name: 2 John
description: Truth and love · received teaching · limits of welcome · shared joy

1.text: The elder, to the chosen lady and her children, whom I love in truth, and not I only, but also all those who know the truth,
for the truth’s sake, which remains in us, and it will be with us forever:
Grace, mercy, and peace will be with us, from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
I rejoice greatly that I have found some of your children walking in truth, even as we have been commanded by the Father.
Now I beg you, dear lady, not as though I wrote to you a new commandment, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another.
This is love, that we should walk according to his commandments. This is the commandment, even as you heard from the beginning, that you should walk in it.
For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who don’t confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh. This is the deceiver and the Antichrist.
Watch yourselves, that we don’t lose the things which we have accomplished, but that we receive a full reward.
Whoever transgresses and doesn’t remain in the teaching of Christ doesn’t have God. He who remains in the teaching has both the Father and the Son.
If anyone comes to you and doesn’t bring this teaching, don’t receive him into your house, and don’t welcome him,
for he who welcomes him participates in his evil deeds.
Having many things to write to you, I don’t want to do so with paper and ink, but I hope to come to you and to speak face to face, that our joy may be made full.
The children of your chosen sister greet you. Amen.

chapters.title: Love and truth shape the limits of welcome during a teaching conflict
chapters.summary: The elder writes to the chosen lady and her children. He rejoices that some of her children walk in truth. He asks that they love one another, as commanded from the beginning. Love means walking by God’s commandments. Many deceivers deny that Jesus Christ came in the flesh. Whoever goes beyond Christ’s teaching does not have God. They should not receive such a teacher into the house. The elder hopes to come and speak face to face.
chapters.meaning: Verse 5 asks for love and says the command is not new. Verse 6 defines the word: love is walking by his commandments. The command is the one heard from the beginning. That definition prepares for verse 7, where deceivers bring a different teaching. Verse 10 then limits welcome. A house should not receive one who does not bring Christ’s teaching.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson uses this warning to discuss remaining in Christ's teaching. How does walking in received teaching connect love with responsible welcome?

chapters.historicalNote: The elder connects the opening affection with truth that remains among the hearers. The USCCB introduction reads the chosen lady and her children as a specific assembly. This interpretation does not establish a named woman or an exact place. The command to love then becomes walking in received teaching rather than affection alone. Refused welcome concerns visitors who deny Christ's coming in flesh and spread that contrary message. The ending seeks conversation in person, showing that written warnings serve an ongoing relationship.
